# FDG5002

> DO NOT arbitrarily vary parameter names in overloads. If a parameter in one overload represents the same input as a parameter in another overload, the parameters should have the same name.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.1.1 Member Overloading.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Not an analyzer candidate: whether two parameters represent the same input is a matter of meaning, so a check by type and position would guess. CA1725 compares the parameter names of an override with its base declaration, not overloads with each other, so it is not mapped. FDG5003 checks that parameters with the same name keep their position.

## From the book

```csharp
public class String {
   // correct
   public int IndexOf (string value) { ... }
   public int IndexOf (string value, int startIndex) { ... }

   // incorrect
   public int IndexOf (string value) { ... }
   public int IndexOf (string str, int startIndex) { ... }
}
```
